sections.content: How many people are "chemical and related process operatives"?

27,040 people

were counted on the census as "chemical and related process operatives" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Chemical and related process operatives operate machinery in the processing of chemical and related materials by chemical, heat or other treatment. This work can relate to the manufacture of synthetic materials and bleach, dyeing or otherwise treating textiles, and treating hides, skins and pelts for making into fur, leather and skin products.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "chemical and related process operatives" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "chemical and related process operatives", 13.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "chemical and related process operatives" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "chemical and related process operatives" included:

  • process operatives (other)
  • plastics process operatives
  • electrical and electronic trades (other)

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "chemical and related process operatives" there were more men than women (79.1% compared with 20.9%).

This means "chemical and related process operatives" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "process, plant and machine operatives".

Men made up 79.1% and women made up 20.9% of "chemical and related process operatives"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "chemical and related process operatives" included:

  • caretakers
  • printing machine assistants
  • production managers and directors in manufacturing

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "chemical and related process operatives" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "chemical and related process operatives" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "chemical and related process operatives", 8.2% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (92.5% compared with 7.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (95.2%) than self-employed (4.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the North West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Cheshire West and Chester, this is in the same region of the North West.
